title: Chopin, Étude Op. 25 No. 5: Neeman and Goldstein
work: Étude in E minor, Op. 25 No. 5
question: Goldstein, on an Érard of 1851, and Neeman play the étude’s semitone clashes and its slower middle section in E major.
intro: Chopin’s tune repeatedly sounds the adjacent semitone before reaching its note. Goldstein and Neeman move from these quick semitone clashes to a slower song in E major, low in the piano. The opening then returns with its clipped chords.

recordings.label: Edward Neeman, c. 2014
recordings.note: Neeman’s teacher Larry Sitsky wrote his First Piano Sonata for him; Neeman made its first recording.

recordings.label: Martha Goldstein
recordings.note: Goldstein’s Érard was built in Paris in 1851 and restored with its original hammers and action.

passages.label: Opening with semitone clashes
passages.note: Quick semitone clashes interrupt the tune. The opening has short, clipped chords and brief pauses.

passages.label: Middle section in E major
passages.note: In E major, the left hand plays a broad melody while the right hand moves up and down around it.

passages.label: Return of the E minor opening
passages.note: The quick E minor opening returns after the long central song, with its short phrases and semitone steps.

sources.title: Mieczysław Tomaszewski, Chopin Institute — the scherzando opening, cello-like middle melody and return
Op. 25 No. 5 — semitone dissonances, E major middle section and return
